title: StockSelectionRequestV1
description: A stock selection in one of two modes. `criteria` is a query over a region's universe: filters are ANDed, `sort` orders the matches and `limit` caps the page at 100 rows. `symbols` is an explicit ticker list resolved inside the universe addressed by `snapshot_id`, in request order, with its own `limit`. The response carries `total` (every row that matched) separately from `returned` (the page), so a 100-row panel never claims to be a 100-stock market. A filter key may be one of the 83 filter keys (`x-filter-keys`) or one of the catalogue spellings in `x-filter-aliases` (`pe`, `roic`, `market_cap`); both are resolved to one row column, and a key no column can answer is a 422 that names it. The two tables together are the vocabulary a filter picker is built from. `criteria.sort` orders by any comparable row column — its own name (`pe_ttm`), the catalogue/UI spelling the screener sends (`perf_4w`, `pe`, `sma50`, `company`) or a legacy name (`gainers`) — with `-field` ascending; a text column sorts alphabetically and `no` is client-only and refused. The top-level `signal` narrows the whole query to one of the signal populations. `GET /screens/filters` publishes the Descriptive group itself — every control, its options, its availability and the predicate each option compiles to — so a panel never hardcodes a vocabulary the server owns.

mode.description: Which question is being asked; the two modes share no knobs.

region.description: Criteria only: the universe tab to query.

signal.description: Criteria only: one of the 27 signals. 22 can run here (top-gainers, top-losers, most-active, most-volatile, most-increased-volume, unusual-volume, overbought, oversold, new-high, new-low, wedgeup, wedge, wedgedown, tri-ascending, tri-descending, channelup, channel, channeldown, doubletop, doublebottom, head-shoulders, head-shoulders-inverse); the other 5 are a 422 `unavailable_signal` naming the metric they would need (analyst revisions, an earnings session stamp, the news store, chart-pattern detection). A signal sets the **population**, and when `criteria.sort` is absent its own measure becomes the order (`top-losers` ascends); an explicit sort always wins. A `symbols` selection does not take it.

asset_class.description: Both modes: the instrument family. `stock` (default) and `etf` are different universes — `us_etf` implies `etf`, and `global` is stock-only. The ETF universe is `type=fund` + `subtype=etf` with no market-cap floor and the same OTC exclusion.

view.description: Both modes: shape every response row as one of the six views. A viewed row carries `rank`/`symbol`/`as_of` plus one cell per declared view column, filled from the parity metrics the bulk scan carries (missing columns stay null, never 0); without `view` the row is the light screen row.

columns.description: Both modes: the exact cells each row returns, in order. `symbol` and `as_of` are always present; a requested cell the row does not carry is null. Omit it for the historical light row. `logo` is an accepted column name (a vendored asset path or an offline monogram data URI) and is the one cell that is opt-in: a 100-row panel that did not ask for it does not carry 100 base64 marks. Mutually exclusive with `view` — two ways to name the same output is a question with two answers.

limit.description: Symbols only: the page size for a ticker lookup, which has no `criteria` block to carry it. Clamped to 100, exactly like `criteria.limit`. A criteria query sends its limit inside `criteria`; a second answer at the top level is a 422.

fill_wide.description: Both modes: opt-in display enrichment for the wide table. Reads page-only cells such as employees, IPO and insider transactions from the stock page after the selection has been answered. A missing cell stays null; this never changes which rows match.

filters.description: ANDed predicates; an empty list is the identity. A key with no light row column is refused with a 422 naming the missing metric — never ignored, because an ignored filter returns the unfiltered screen.

sort.description: The one metric the page is ordered by: any comparable catalog column, descending, or `-<field>` for ascending (the panel's own `o=-marketcap`). A column may be named by its row field (`ret_1m`), by the catalogue/UI spelling the screener sends (`perf_4w`, `pe`, `sma50`, `company`, `ticker`) or by a legacy name (`market_cap`, `turnover`, `gainers`); every spelling resolves to the same column. A text column sorts alphabetically (A-Z / Z-A), and a missing value sorts last in both directions. `no` is client-only — the row number comes from the page offset — and an unknown spelling is a 422 `unknown_sort` naming the accepted fields. When `signal` is named and this is absent, the signal's own measure becomes the order; an explicit sort always wins.

limit.description: Page size. Clamped to 100: a larger value is not an error, it simply cannot widen the panel, and the response reports the limit that was applied.

offset.description: Zero-based row offset after filtering and sorting. The response still reports the full post-filter total, so 20-row pages can walk the whole universe.

common_only.description: Display-only switch: keep the common-stock universe and leave preferred/warrant lines out of the page.

entitlement.description: The tier this request asks to be judged at. It can only **narrow** the caller's plan — resolved from the `x-plan` header or from the plan the `x-api-key` key carries, with `free` for an anonymous caller. A request naming a tier above its plan is a 403 `premium_required`, and so is any filter key whose tier in app/screen/data/entitlements.json is `premium` while the request's entitlement is `free`: refused by name, never answered with an empty page and never silently downgraded. Omit it to be judged at the plan.

symbols.description: Symbols only: tickers in the order the response should list them. A ticker the universe does not carry is reported in `missing`.

source.description: Symbols only: the provenance the snapshot must declare. A source the snapshot was not built from is refused, never relabelled.

snapshot_id.description: Symbols only: the snapshot whose region and rule version the tickers are resolved against. It fixes *which* universe, not the prices — the rows are read fresh and dated by the response's `as_of`, never by the snapshot's.

filter.description: One predicate: exactly one of `key` (a filter key, resolved to its row column) or `field` (the column itself), plus an operator and a value. A key whose entry in `x-filter-keys` carries `choice` takes `op: eq` and an option token as `value`; a key whose entry carries `bucket` also takes one of its named bucket ids that way (`price:u5`, `cap:mega`, `idx:sp500`), and `GET /screens/filters` publishes every id with the predicate it compiles to.

key.description: One of the 83 filter keys. The 49 that resolve to one row column, the 3 that filter through their option vocabulary, the 25 bucket-only key (sh_opt, ipodate, idx, fa_epsyoy, fa_epsyoy1, fa_epsqoq, fa_epsyoyttm, fa_eps3years, fa_eps5years, fa_estltgrowth, fa_salesqoq, fa_salesyoyttm, fa_sales3years, fa_sales5years, fa_divgrowth, sh_insttrans, fa_epsrev, ta_highlow50d, ta_alltime, ta_candlestick, ah_close, ah_change, news_date, news_keywords, etf_heldby) that filters through a named bucket, and the 6 that are refused with their reason, are listed in x-filter-keys. A filter may also name one of the 138 catalogue spellings in x-filter-aliases (`pe`, `roic`, `market_cap`), each published with the row column it means; the two tables together are the 221 keys a filter may name, and any other key is a 422 that names it.

value.description: The comparison value. `in` and `between` take an array (`between` exactly two numbers); every other operator takes one scalar. For an option-driven key (ta_perf, ta_perf2, ta_volatility) the value is the source-panel option token itself (`1w10u`, `dup`, `wo2`), and the predicate each token compiles to is published under `x-filter-keys.<key>.choice.options`. For a key whose entry carries `bucket: true` the value is one of the bucket ids that key publishes (`price:u5`, `cap:mega`, `idx:sp500`), with `op: eq`; the predicate each id runs is in `GET /screens/filters` and in the key's own `x-filter-keys` entry. For `exch` the value is a MIC (`XNAS`, `XNYS`, `XASE`, `XCBO`) or one of the spellings published under `x-filter-keys.exch.aliases`; any other value on the US tabs is a 422 `unknown_value` whose message lists the accepted codes, while a non-US region (`global`) accepts a provider code matching `[A-Z0-9]{1,8}` (e.g. `SIX`, `XLON`) and answers with the rows it names — zero when it names none. Everywhere else the source panel's option tokens (`mega`, `u5`, `ob70`) are display buckets, not values: send the number the bucket means.

sh_trades.label: Trades
sh_trades.reason: no trade-count feed; Finra publishes short-sale volume, not trade counts — the scan carries volume in shares and turnover in currency, the depth store has no print count, and deriving a trade count from volume would be a fabricated number (Polygon.io aggregates, IEX HIST or Databento would answer it). The control is premium-tier like the rest of the source panel's paid set; this refusal is about the missing feed, not about the tier

theme.label: Theme
theme.reason: needs theme/sub-theme classification: no layer carries a theme column — not the scan, not the depth store's 106 cells, not the snapshot, not SQLite — so the source panel's 40 theme and 268 sub-theme tokens name a taxonomy nothing in this deployment speaks

subtheme.label: Sub-theme
subtheme.reason: needs theme/sub-theme classification: no layer carries a theme column — not the scan, not the depth store's 106 cells, not the snapshot, not SQLite — so the source panel's 40 theme and 268 sub-theme tokens name a taxonomy nothing in this deployment speaks

sh_insidertrans.label:
Insider
Transactions
sh_insidertrans.reason: reads a mixture of ownership levels and junk (TSLA 76.0, META 45.9, GME 8.7): the depth cell is a vendor net-change nobody can read as a flow, so the product withdrew the control by name rather than publish an interpretation the data does not support

choice.grammar: <window><direction>: windows d, 1w, 4w, 13w, 26w, ytd, 52w, 3y, 5y, 10y; directions up, down, <N>u (down at least N percent), <N>o (up at least N percent)
<window><direction>: windows d, 1w, 4w, 13w, 26w, ytd, 52w, 3y, 5y, 10y; directions up, down, <N>u (down at least N percent), <N>o (up at least N percent)
<wo|mo><N>: weekly (wo) or monthly (mo) volatility of at least N percent

ta_highlow20d.label: 20-Day High/Low
ta_highlow20d.reason: needs a 20-day high/low column: the scan carries the 52-week extremes and the depth store carries the 50-day ones, so a 50-day figure cannot be narrowed to 20 days

ta_pattern.label: Pattern
ta_pattern.reason: needs a chart-pattern detector: the depth store's `candlestick_pattern` flag has three classes (doji/engulfing/hammer) but no price series, and the source panel's 28 chart-pattern tokens need daily bars to detect — no bars store is ingested

x-entitlement.note: Tier is configured in app/screen/data/entitlements.json, not in code: a feature set to `free` there is answered to every caller on the next request. A premium feature the deployment cannot source is still refused by its own reason (x-filter-keys.<key>.reason) — tier and availability are different facts.
